modelNotes: Minutes Engine 1.1 uses player-pool status plus season, last 5, and last 10 minutes from NBA history.
Unknown starters retain their historical minutes baseline and are not treated as confirmed bench players.
Missing injury information does not mean a player is cleared; publication eligibility requires confirmed game status and role.
Roles are Core Starter, Starter, Rotation, Bench, Deep Bench, and Inactive.
No odds or betting lines are used.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
injury.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

injury.shortComment: Williamson is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs due to a left thigh contusion.
injury.detail: Williamson won't suit up Saturday on the second leg of this back-to-back set. Derik Queen will start in his place alongside Yves Missi in the frontcourt. This will be Williamson's second absence this season. The 26-year-old is averaging 21.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals across 32.4 minutes per outing in 16 regular-season games.

injury.shortComment: White (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Sacramento.
injury.detail: White drew the questionable tag for Saturday's game due to left AC joint sprain in his shoulder. The veteran guard will be in street clothes for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, but he could make his return Sunday against the Warriors. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also out, Payton Pritchard and Paul George will carry the workload for the Celtics, and there will be more opportunities for the likes of Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Tatum (rest) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings.
injury.detail: Tatum will be rested for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, so he should be back on the floor for Sunday's game against the Warriors. With both Tatum and Derrick White (shoulder) sidelined, the Celtics will rely more heavily on Paul George, Payton Pritchard, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser to carry the scoring load against Sacramento.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
injury.detail: Robinson is under the weather and will not play in the front end of Boston's back-to-back set, but he could be available for Sunday night's game against the Warriors. With Robinson sidelined, Luka Garza and Chris Cenac should both see a bump in minutes behind starting center Neemias Queta.

injury.shortComment: Bona (back) participated in Friday's practice, though he still needs to go through a full practice with contact before being cleared to return to game action, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
injury.detail: Bona hasn't played since Nov. 4 due to a back sprain, though he appears to be trending in the right direction. Until the big man is cleared to play, Dominick Barlow (back) and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased minutes.

injury.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injury.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injury.shortComment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injury.shortComment: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injury.detail: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

injury.shortComment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injury.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

injury.shortComment: Ingram (Achilles) is expected to make his season and team debut Monday against the Rockets, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: The star forward is set to make his long-awaited return after undergoing surgery for a partially torn Achilles tendon in May. Ingram, who'll miss Saturday's game in Dallas, is likely to carry a minutes restriction following a lengthy layoff, though his presence is certain to cut into the playing time of the likes of Kris Dunn, Max Strus and Gradey Dick on the wing for the Clippers.

injury.shortComment: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injury.detail: McGowens will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. He's without a timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week until the Pelicans offer an update on his status.

injury.shortComment: Boozer is out for Saturday's game against Minnesota due to a right ankle sprain.
injury.detail: The rookie sensation is sitting out for the first time this year and can be deemed day-to-day for the time being. His absence puts a ton of pressure on Ty Jerome (hip), who's set to return from a three-game layoff, and opens up a spot in the starting lineup likely for Isaiah Stewart.

injury.shortComment: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
injury.detail: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Wade (hamstring) won't play Saturday against the Bucks.
injury.detail: Wade was able to get through a full practice Friday, but the 76ers' medical staff still isn't quite ready to clear him for game-time action. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Trail Blazers. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker will continue to help pick up the slack while Wade is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injury.detail: Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

injury.shortComment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injury.shortComment: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injury.detail: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

injury.shortComment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injury.detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

injury.shortComment: Small won't play Saturday against the Timberwolves due to personal reasons.
injury.detail: It's unclear exactly what Small is dealing with, but for now, he can be considered questionable for Monday's meeting in Charlotte. With Small out, Cam Spencer and Jahmai Mashack will fill the minutes behind Ty Jerome.

injury.shortComment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injury.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injury.shortComment: Brown (hamstring) went through individual work during Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: Brown is set to be re-evaluated this weekend due to a left hamstring strain, meaning his next chance to play will come Monday against Portland. Dean Wade (hamstring), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker are all candidates for increased minutes while Brown is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
injury.detail: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

injury.shortComment: Grant (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
injury.detail: Grant went down early in Thursday's win over the Warriors, and he's now dealing with a strained left calf that could cost him multiple contests. With Cameron Boozer (ankle) also sidelined, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper are both worthy of streaming consideration in fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Clarkson (foot) won't play in Saturday's game against Portland.
injury.detail: Clarkson is battling a case of plantar fasciitis in his right foot, so he will miss a second consecutive contest. Without Clarkson on the floor, Landry Shamet is in line for more playing time.

injury.shortComment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injury.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injury.shortComment: Towns (illness) won't play in Saturday's game versus the Trail Blazers.
injury.detail: Towns was initially listed as questionable. However, he has since been ruled out, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. Towns' next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Indiana. In the meantime, Andre Drummond is in line to start.

injury.shortComment: Anunoby (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers.
injury.detail: Anunoby will miss his first game of the 2026-27 regular season due to left calf tightness, although he could be back on the floor for the second leg of the Knicks' back-to-back set against the Pacers on Sunday. Landry Shamet and Miles McBride are both in line for elevated roles in Anunoby's absence.

injury.shortComment: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
injury.detail: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

injury.shortComment: Washington (illness/shoulder) is listed as out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injury.detail: Washington was initially listed on the injury report due to a shoulder issue. Since then, he developed an illness and was downgraded to doubtful. Washington will now miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign, with his next opportunity to play coming Sunday in Utah. In the meantime, Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher are candidates for more minutes.

injury.shortComment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injury.shortComment: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
injury.detail: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injury.shortComment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

injury.shortComment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

injury.shortComment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Lawal (groin) is out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injury.detail: Lawal will miss a second straight game with right groin tightness. The rookie forward isn't expected to have a big role in the rotation, so he likely won't have much fantasy upside anytime soon. His next chance to play will come Sunday against the Jazz on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

injury.shortComment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injury.detail: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

injury.shortComment: Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
injury.detail: Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

injury.shortComment: Murphy (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
injury.detail: Murphy missed six consecutive games due to bilateral patellar tendinopathy before returning for Friday's game against the Thunder, when he played 29 minutes and finished with 17 points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block in a 126-120 loss for the Pelicans. He'll sit for the second leg of a back-to-back set, which means more minutes will be available for Jordan Poole, Herbert Jones and Derik Queen. Murphy's next opportunity to play is Monday against the Suns.

injury.shortComment: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injury.detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

injury.shortComment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injury.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injury.detail: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.
